title: Manage the data lifecycle: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: At this data state, what purpose, copy, owner, protection, retention, and transition evidence must be true?
focalInsight: Lifecycle decisions follow data across recipients, replicas, archives, backups, and destruction scope.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Data Lifecycle
nodes.definition: Managed journey of data from collection/creation through use, sharing, storage, archive, and destruction.
nodes.detail: Managed journey of data from collection/creation through use, sharing, storage, archive, and destruction.
nodes.decision: Set owner, purpose, location, access, retention, transition evidence at each state.
nodes.failureExample: Application deletion leaves snapshots and exports active.

nodes.label: Collection
nodes.definition: Obtaining, generating, observing, or receiving data for a stated purpose.
nodes.detail: Obtaining, generating, observing, or receiving data for a stated purpose.
nodes.decision: Set purpose, data elements, authority, source, quality, classification, recipient, retention.
nodes.failureExample: Team collects precise location data without need or retention trigger.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Collection begins before the first database record.

nodes.label: Use
nodes.definition: Authorized processing of data for defined purpose and role.
nodes.detail: Authorized processing of data for defined purpose and role.
nodes.decision: Check purpose, access, transformation, output, and audit evidence.
nodes.failureExample: Support staff repurpose customer data for analytics without authority.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Use must remain within approved purpose.

nodes.label: Sharing
nodes.definition: Providing data to another internal or external recipient or channel.
nodes.detail: Providing data to another internal or external recipient or channel.
nodes.decision: Check recipient role, minimum data, transfer path, contract, location, safeguards, evidence.
nodes.failureExample: Vendor receives full dataset when only aggregate data is needed.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Sharing changes the trust and control boundary.

nodes.label: Archival
nodes.definition: Retaining data still needed but less active under preserved access and integrity controls.
nodes.detail: Retaining data still needed but less active under preserved access and integrity controls.
nodes.decision: Set retention basis, readability, metadata, access, preservation, and retrieval evidence.
nodes.failureExample: Backup is called archive though no record purpose or retrieval control exists.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Archive is not destruction or ordinary backup.

nodes.label: Destruction
nodes.definition: Authorized end-state action rendering data/media no longer available as required by policy and method.
nodes.detail: Authorized end-state action rendering data/media no longer available as required by policy and method.
nodes.decision: Confirm trigger, hold status, scope/copies, method, verification, validation, evidence.
nodes.failureExample: Visible record is deleted while replicas and backups remain.

nodes.label: Data Minimization
nodes.definition: Limiting data and precision to what purpose requires.
nodes.detail: Limiting data and precision to what purpose requires.
nodes.decision: Review purpose when source, recipient, or use changes.
nodes.failureExample: Derived dataset keeps unnecessary identifiers indefinitely.
